junior.what: The spleen is a soft, fist-sized organ in the upper left of the abdomen, behind the stomach.
junior.does: It filters the blood, removing worn-out red blood cells, and it is a base for white blood cells that fight infections.
junior.funFact: The spleen keeps a store of platelets and white blood cells, ready to help heal injuries and fight germs.
junior.details: The spleen is part of the lymphatic system, the body's defence team. People can live without a spleen, but they may catch some infections more easily.

junior.what: The thymus is a small gland in the chest, behind the breastbone and in front of the heart.
junior.does: It trains white blood cells called T cells to recognise germs and to leave the body's own cells alone.
junior.funFact: The thymus is largest in children and slowly shrinks after puberty.
junior.details: It also makes a hormone, thymosin, so it belongs to both the immune system and the endocrine system.
